entities.name: HCV-related cirrhosis
observations: Chronic HCV with low albumin, prolonged INR, thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, and spider telangiectasias supports advanced cirrhosis with portal hypertension.
Patients with HCV-related cirrhosis require hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance and assessment for gastroesophageal varices.

entities.name: HCC surveillance
observations: For established HCV-related cirrhosis, liver ultrasound every 6 months with serum AFP is recommended; routine CT or MRI is not the primary surveillance strategy.
Multiphasic CT or contrast MRI is reserved for suspicious ultrasound findings, abnormal or rising AFP, or inadequate ultrasound visualization.

entities.name: Variceal screening
observations: Thrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, spider telangiectasias, low albumin, and prolonged INR indicate portal hypertension; screening EGD is indicated unless validated noninvasive rule-out criteria apply.
This patient is unlikely to meet low-risk criteria for avoiding EGD.

entities.name: PMID: HCC and variceal screening evidence
observations: Search-agent evidence supports combined HCC surveillance with ultrasound plus AFP and screening EGD for portal-hypertensive varices in this clinical scenario.
